page_title: Lessons Learned from Twenty Years of Site Reliability Engineering

sources.entry: Lessons learned from two decades of Site Reliability Engineering

summary.title: Lessons Learned from Twenty Years of Site Reliability Engineering
summary.one_liner: Eleven reliability lessons from Google SRE's two decades of running large distributed systems, drawn from real outages such as the 2016 YouTube caching outage and the 2017 OAuth token incident.
takeaways: Match the riskiness of an incident mitigation to the severity of the outage, since a risky fix can make things worse.
Test recovery mechanisms and mitigations before an emergency, and canary all changes with progressive rollouts.
Give every service dependency a 'big red button', keep backup communication channels that do not depend on production services, and automate known mitigations to cut MTTR.
Combine unit tests with integration tests, and test disaster resilience and recovery, not just normal operation.
Shorter gaps between rollouts and diverse infrastructure reduce surprises from latent bugs and single points of failure.
summary.summary: The page is a Google SRE retrospective, written by a team of Google SRE authors, that lists eleven lessons learned over two decades of site reliability engineering. Each lesson is tied to a specific incident, such as a 2016 YouTube caching outage, a 2017 OAuth token failure that logged out millions of users, a 2023 networking failure, and a 2020 device bug that caused a regional outage. The lessons cover mitigation risk, testing and canarying, rollout cadence, automation, graceful degradation, and avoiding single points of failure. It is written as a narrative with short explanations rather than a formal tutorial.
